visual_goal: Show the migration safety net: intercepted data access, reads ramped behind a gate on two paths with comparison, shadow writes, and change data capture feeding derived stores.
prompt: A simple left-to-right diagram with six elements. At the left, an old block building labeled Monolith. In the middle-left, a dial-shaped gate labeled Read gate. In the middle-right, two items stacked: a small new service box labeled Homes service on top and a database cylinder labeled Old database below. At the far right, a large magnifying glass labeled Compare. Along the top edge, centered, a pale ghostly database cylinder labeled Shadow writes. Arrows: one from Monolith to Read gate; one from Read gate to Homes service; one from Read gate to Old database; one from Homes service to Compare; one from Old database to Compare; one curving from Monolith up and right into Shadow writes; one from Shadow writes down-right into Compare. Exactly seven arrows. Labels are plain text with no quotation marks.
alt: The monolith's reads pass a ramped gate to both a new homes service and the old database, with results compared; its writes go to a shadow database that is also compared.

visual_goal: Show the 2025-2026 layering: apps, server-driven UI, one central data schema, service blocks, data services, change events and derived views.
prompt: A top-to-bottom layered stack drawn as horizontal slabs with one arrow between each pair. Top slab: three small device icons (laptop, two phones) labeled 'Web and apps'. Next slab: 'Server-driven UI'. Next, a wide slab drawn as a connected web of nodes labeled 'Central data schema'. Next, a slab holding three grouped boxes each behind a small door, labeled 'Service blocks'. Next, a slab of database cylinders labeled 'Data services'. To the right of the data services, one arrow labeled 'change events' flows into a pipe, which flows into a final box at the lower right labeled 'Derived views'. Six arrows in total, all pointing downward or to the right.
alt: A layered stack from web and apps through server-driven UI, a central data schema, service blocks and data services, with change events flowing into derived views.

visual_goal: Show the money cycle: guest pays a licensed entity, funds held until check-in, then fee recognized and host paid, with refunds and three-way reconciliation.
prompt: A left-to-right money flow. At the left, an unlabeled generic guest with a phone sends one arrow labeled 'pays' into a plain building labeled 'Licensed entity'. That building sends one arrow into a central open ledger book on a safe, labeled 'Ledger', with a small padlock showing funds held. A small calendar page beside the ledger is labeled 'check-in'. From the ledger, three arrows fan out to the right: upper arrow to a small coin pile labeled 'Fee revenue', middle arrow to a small house with a host labeled 'Host payout', lower arrow to a returning-coin icon labeled 'Refund or claim'. Below the ledger, a stack of a document and a bank statement labeled 'Bank and processor records' sends one arrow up into the ledger labeled 'reconcile'. Exactly six arrows.
alt: A guest pays a licensed entity; funds are held in a ledger until check-in, then flow to fee revenue, the host payout or a refund, while bank and processor records reconcile against the ledger.
